clue.text: Resorting to the war, there's trouble getting into it

indicators.note: re-sorting the letters means putting them into a fresh order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who resorts to war finds they have landed themselves in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resorting' reads as 'turning to' but splits as re-sorting, shuffling TO THE WAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in hot water is an idiom for being in trouble, so it is trouble one gets into.

clue.text: Man, say, offering yarn with no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the first letter of the yarn word is dropped

parts.note: lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread or yarn

explanation.surface: A man spins a story without bothering to introduce it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, an example of the word for an island.

clue.text: Victoria was not Posh Spice initially (synthetically made exterior)

indicators.note: exterior says the rearranged letters form an outside layer around the rest
synthetically suggests something artificially built up, so these letters are reconstructed

parts.note: U is the classic shorthand for upper-class, posh usage

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word Spice

explanation.surface: A remark about Victoria Beckham, once Posh Spice, with a parenthetical aside about something manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously quoted 'We are not amused'; the surface points to Victoria Beckham instead. U and S sit inside AMED, the anagram of MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: The attributed quotation 'We are not amused' makes this the word Queen Victoria was not.

clue.text: Separate urinals out of order

indicators.note: out of order describes letters no longer in their proper sequence, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice on public toilets that are broken and set apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means cut off or isolated, as an island is, hence separate.

clue.text: Model cast out during slanging match returned to adulterer

parts.note: the Ford Model T supplies the letter T

indicators.note: returned means the combined piece is read backwards
during says one piece occurs in the middle of the other

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel or slanging match
to emit is to give off or cast out

explanation.surface: A fashion model, thrown out mid-argument, goes back to a cheating partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model but is the Ford Model T; 'returned' reverses REMITOW, the emission inside the quarrel, to WOTIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer is someone unfaithful to a partner, a cheat in love.

clue.text: Dictator offered nothing for it: chap ravaged by kind of disease with no known cause

definitions.text: kind of disease with no known cause

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda
O looks like a zero, nothing

indicators.note: ravaged suggests being torn apart and wrecked, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tyrant finds nothing to offer, while some fellow is laid waste by a mysterious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ravaged' scrambles the letters of 'it' and 'chap'. Idi Amin was Uganda's dictator in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiopathic is the medical term for a disorder arising spontaneously, without any identifiable origin.

clue.text: Processed credit details stolen

definitions.meaning: a credit card is processed by swiping it through a reader
to swipe is slang for to steal

explanation.definitionFit: Swiping a card reads its details, and swiping is also informal for pinching something.

clue.text: Those up and off seem restrained by instrument

indicators.note: restrained by says the rearranged letters are held inside the instrument

parts.note: a horn is a brass musical instrument

indicators.note: off describes something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Those who get up and leave look as if held back by some musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles 'seem'. Riders are said to be 'up' when mounted, so 'Those up' are not people who have risen from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders are 'up' when mounted on a horse, so those up are the riders on horseback.

clue.text: Drag character or characters from "www.", one entered with an "enter", perhaps

indicators.note: entered says one piece is placed inside the other
characters from means the letters of the prefix are taken and rearranged

parts.note: the web-address prefix is spelt out as three Ws and a dot
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
Enter is a key on a computer keyboard, 'perhaps' marking it as an example

explanation.surface: Talk of web addresses and keyboard keys, dressed up as a riddle about typing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters from' shuffles the prefix's letters to WDOWTW, with I after its first W. Widow Twankey is the pantomime dame in Aladdin, a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime dame role is traditionally played by a man dressed as a woman, a drag character.

clue.text: Precious time, minute

parts.note: minute (my-NEWT) means tiny, which is wee

explanation.surface: Time is precious, even a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like sixty seconds, but here it is the adjective meaning very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious can mean affectedly dainty, the same as twee.

clue.text: United team from London area going round North playing in knockout competition

indicators.note: going round says the London area surrounds the rest

parts.note: SE is the postcode for south-east London

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout tournament

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are at play, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football club from the capital goes north to play in a cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' scrambles 'North' to NTHOR. Scunthorpe United is an English football club; 'United' looks like a description but belongs to the club's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scunthorpe United is a football club known by its town name, so a United team.

clue.text: To leave someone helpless is the London way

definitions.meaning: to leave them stuck with no means of getting away
a famous street in central London

explanation.definitionFit: Stranding someone leaves them stuck, and the Strand is a major thoroughfare in the West End.

clue.text: To improve morale, I eat tripe

indicators.note: tripe is rubbish or nonsense, so the letters are made into a mess

explanation.surface: Eating offal as a morale booster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like food but signals nonsense, reordering MORALE I EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is a formal word for making something better.

clue.text: They provide inflated support for team restricted by …

indicators.note: restricted by says the team is held within the arms

parts.note: the ellipsis stands for the next answer, an arsenal, which is a store of arms
a band is a group of people working together, a team

explanation.surface: Something gives buoyant support to a team which is hemmed in by what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the reader into 15 across: its answer, an arsenal, is a store of weapons, ARMS, which hold BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable armbands keep a learner swimmer afloat, giving support filled with air.

clue.text: … side of meat, but no starter, with side's sides inside

indicators.note: inside says those letters go within the shortened word
no starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: carnal means relating to the flesh, of meat

indicators.note: sides picks the first and last letters of the word side

explanation.surface: A butcher's side of meat, missing its first course, with the flanks tucked in.
explanation.walkthrough: CARNAL loses its first letter to give ARNAL, and S and E, the first and last letters of 'side', go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a London football club, and a club team is a side.

clue.text: No head to visit comprehensive

indicators.note: no head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: to call round is to visit someone

explanation.surface: An instruction never to visit the head teacher of a comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehensive' looks like a British state school but is the adjective for wide-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: All-round means covering every aspect, thorough and comprehensive.

clue.text: Ham stirred into cereal for Hindu

indicators.note: into says the mixed letters go inside the cereal

parts.note: bran is a cereal product

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: stir ham into your breakfast cereal, though the diner is Hindu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' scrambles 'Ham' to AHM; a Hindu would of course not eat ham, which adds to the surface's oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brahman is a member of the highest, priestly caste of Hindus.

clue.text: A sort of hatred

parts.note: a version is a sort or kind of something

explanation.surface: A description of some form of loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but 'A sort' gives the wordplay and 'of' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, close to hatred.

clue.text: See 9
Relative with child in Spain entering non-English principality sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole construction is read backwards
entering says the child goes inside the principality
non-English means E, for English, is removed

parts.note: Wales is a principality of the UK
nino is Spanish for child

explanation.surface: A relative and a youngster from Spain travel into Wales and are later sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses WALNINOS, the whole construction, to give the answer read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A son-in-law is a relative by marriage, a daughter's husband.

clue.text: Being decapitated, disturbs rest

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: to bother someone is to disturb them

explanation.surface: Someone's beheading disturbs the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like sleep, but it is the noun for the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest means the remaining ones, the others.

clue.text: Paul's the self-proclaimed Son of God, held to be name taken in jest

indicators.note: held says the man is held inside the setter's word

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so the setter's means my
David Icke, the conspiracy theorist, announced in 1991 that he was a son of God

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be the Son of God, though this is taken as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Paul's' means the setter's, MY.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the mickey is a British idiom for teasing someone, so the mickey is what is taken in jest.

clue.text: These days on the border there's chaos

parts.note: May is a month, a run of days
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Nowadays there is disorder along the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These days' looks like 'nowadays', but it is a set of days, the month of May.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem means violent disorder, chaos.

clue.text: Careful Italian woman imbibed drink

indicators.note: imbibed says one piece swallows the other

parts.note: chary means wary or careful
donna is Italian for woman or lady

explanation.surface: A cautious Italian lady has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Chary is an old-fashioned word for cautious, which the surface hides as 'Careful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a white wine grape and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Autumn weather yearned for, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: something yearned for is missed

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the seasonal weather of autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is low cloud typical of autumn mornings, so a kind of autumn weather.

clue.text: Small child with strength attended to

indicators.note: attended to means listened to, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: might means power or strength

explanation.surface: A little one with plenty of vigour, looked after carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attended to' looks like 'cared for' but means listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Mite is an affectionate term for a small child.

clue.text: Sell down the river, not a river on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run across these words is a coincidence of the abbreviation, not a hidden run

explanation.surface: Betrayal is described, with the reassurance that no river is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read a hidden word, but no word signals hiding: NOT, A and R (river) form NOTAR, which 'on the way back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform against them, a betrayal like selling them down the river.

clue.text: What's put up right to left where right, left and centre put up?

definitions.text: where right, left and centre put up?

indicators.note: right to left says the R for right becomes an L for left

parts.note: an erection is something built or put up

explanation.surface: A riddle about political parties of all stripes putting candidates forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to left' looks like reading backwards, but it swaps R for L in ERECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: In an election candidates of the right, left and centre stand, or are put up.
